submission.natural_language_explanation: The positive pole is a retrospective current-token detector that fires strongly only on a small memorized token set headed by ' interval'/' intervals' (~1.3-1.8) and ' spaced'/' spacing' in any sense including 'spaced out' (~0.9-1.5), plus ' span', ' switch', ' bridge', ' Welcome', ' Guinness' and mid-word fragments such as 'ign' and 'gs' (~0.7-1.0). It stays at or below ~0.43 on near-synonyms ' gap', ' margin', ' ratio', ' boundary', ' strait', ' distance', ' width' and ' clearance' even in identical two-anchor frames; the peak token itself causes the firing and editing anything after the peak has no effect.

Within the U.S., it is estimated that 25 percent of the population use on-site septic tank waste water treatment systems. It is also estimated that 5% of these systems fail each year due to poor maintenance.
Tips for a healthy septic system:
1) Biodegradable waste water only should be discharged in a septic system.
2) Never use a garbage disposal with a septic system. The undigested raw food will inter the system and convert to a bio mat clogging the drain field.
3) Never use anti-bacteria products with a septic system.
4) Never flush sanitary napkins or any other non biodegradable product down a septic tank system.
5) Never dump oil, paints or solvents down a septic system. Not only they damage your septic system, they will also contaminate groundwater lakes and springs.
6) Treat your septic tank with a bacterial septic tank treatment monthly. This will help to digest solids prolonging the life of your septic system.
7) Pump the system every three years.
8) Never plant trees or shrubs over a drain field.
9) Never pave or lay concrete over a septic tank.
10) Never drive over your drain field.
Inspect your system on a monthly basis. Contact your local plumber at the first sign of a wet drain field, septic odors or any sign of blockage. Maintaining your septic tank and drain field will ensure many years of trouble free service.

Los fiscales federales de Boston agilizan la extradición desde Massachusetts a la República Dominicana del dominicano Daniel Emilio Frías Segura, acusado de descuartizar a su esposa en el 2010 y procesado en un tribunal federal de esa ciudad después que fue capturado el jueves de la semana pasada en Lynn (Massachusetts), donde supuestamente se escondía con familiares.
Frías Segura era buscado con una orden de captura internacional que estaba en manos de la Interpol, pero los federales ni la policía de Lynn no han dicho en cuáles circunstancias fue arrestado o si recibieron confidencias que los llevó al lugar en donde se encontraba prófugo.
Medios locales en Massachusetts dijeron el lunes que el fugitivo podría ser enviado tan pronto como se complete una parte del proceso de encausamiento en ese estado. Su estatus migratorio no ha sido abordado en el comunicado oficial.
Aunque el acusado escapó de la República Dominicana a Puerto Rico se cree que entró a Estados Unidos por la frontera con México.
La orden de captura fue emitida el 9 de abril de 2010 por la Procuraduría General de la República Dominicana y los fiscales de Boston no han confirmado si han recibido una petición de extradición antes de la captura de Frías Segura de las autoridades judiciales dominicanas.
Un comunicado del fiscal federal de Boston dice que Frías Segura fue detenido en espera de extradición luego de su comparecencia ante el tribunal.

abstract: 'With the help of various square principles, we obtain results concerning the consistency strength of several statements about trees containing ascent paths, special trees, and strong chain conditions. Building on a result that shows that Todorčević’s principle $\square(\kappa)$ implies an indexed version of $\square(\kappa,\lambda)$, we show that for all infinite, regular cardinals $\lambda<\kappa$, the principle $\square(\kappa)$ implies the existence of a $\kappa$-Aronszajn tree containing a $\lambda$-ascent path. We then provide a complete picture of the consistency strengths of statements relating the interactions of trees with ascent paths and special trees. As a part of this analysis, we construct a model of set theory in which $\aleph_2$-Aronszajn trees exist and all such trees contain $\aleph_0$-ascent paths. Finally, we use our techniques to show that the assumption that the $\kappa$-Knaster property is countably productive and the assumption that every $\kappa$-Knaster partial order is $\kappa$-stationarily layered both imply the failure of $\square(\kappa)$.'

The existence or non-existence of cofinal branches is one of the most fundamental properties of set-theoretic trees[^2] of uncountable regular height.
